summary: Our project, "Harmonizing Heat," is a conceptual educational framework designed to translate complex thermal data from MODIS and VIIRS satellites into simple, accessible infographics. We developed a theoretical platform where users can select a geographical region and instantly view combined, easy-to-understand visual summaries of heat anomalies like wildfires. This directly addresses the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge by bridging the gap between raw Earth Observation data and public comprehension. It is important because it empowers communities, educators, and students to understand changing fire regimes and climate events without needing a technical background in satellite sensor harmonization.
details:
ur project, "Harmonizing Heat," works as a conceptual framework for a digital educational tool. It is designed to take harmonized thermal anomaly data from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite sensors and automatically translate it into simplified, visual storytelling graphics.

The primary benefit is accessibility; raw satellite data can be overwhelming for non-experts. The intended impact of this project is to allow students, educators, and local communities to easily track and understand shifting fire regimes and climate events in their regions. To develop this concept, we utilized standard presentation software to build out the UI/UX mockups and framework. Our team considered the creative angle of "data storytelling"—recognizing that collecting Earth Observation data is only half the battle; the other half is communicating it effectively to the general public without technical jargon.
